name: DIY gap bands

lead: DIY gap bands are small elastic bands that people place around front teeth hoping to close a gap (diastema) and get a more uniform smile without visiting a dentist.

The band is meant to apply inward force so the teeth drift together. In clinics, such forces are applied by supervised appliances, including elastics and springs. The appearance benefit is based on personal accounts, and no research on the home practice was found.

paras: People loop the band around the two teeth beside the gap and leave it in place, with no clinician checking progress.
It has not been studied in published research, and it is done without supervision.

angle.text: Users place small elastic bands around front teeth hoping to close a gap (diastema) and get a more uniform smile without a dentist. The band is meant to pull the teeth together. The benefit is based on personal accounts, and no studies on the method exist.

lead: DIY gap bands are small elastic bands that people place around teeth at home to try to close the gap between the front teeth (a diastema) without seeing a dentist. The aim is a gap-free, more even smile, a change people associate with a neater, more conventionally attractive look, achieved at very low cost.

A diastema is a space between teeth, most often the upper front teeth. Wikipedia lists causes including a prominent lip frenulum, tongue thrusting, gum disease, an extra tooth and a mismatch of jaw growth, and states that a diastema is not a pathology and any treatment is cosmetic; options include orthodontics, bonding, or veneers and crowns [1]. In professional orthodontics, forces are applied to teeth with elastics and springs through fixed appliances that a clinician adjusts [2].
No published studies of the home practice were found, so what the bands do outside clinical supervision has not been described in research.

paras: The practice involves looping a small elastic band around teeth next to a gap so the band pulls them together. It is a home adaptation of the idea behind orthodontic elastics and is usually performed without a dentist.

Diastemata are common in children and can persist into adult teeth, and they occur normally in many mammal species [1]. Causes named by Wikipedia include a lip frenulum that extends between the teeth, tongue thrusting, periodontal bone loss, an extra tooth behind the front teeth, a skeletal mismatch between the jaws and forward-angled front teeth [1]. Because causes differ, treatment in clinics targets the underlying cause and varies by patient [1].

Orthodontic references describe elastics, springs and ligatures as forces applied through fixed appliances under clinician adjustment, and note that springs can be used to close gaps [2]. Wikipedia says fixed appliances give greater mechanical control of teeth and that forces can be applied using elastic bands [2]. It also states that the effectiveness of mail-order clear aligners lacks sufficient evidence [2].
